title: A finite clopen partition extends to Cartier affine charts after admissible blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, and $U=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ a finite partition into quasi-compact subsets open and closed in $U$. There is a $U$-admissible blowup $b:T\to S$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] with $T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and a finite open-and-closed decomposition $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ such that $b^{-1}(U_i)=T_i\cap b^{-1}(U)$. There is a finite affine open cover $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ of $T$, each $W_j$ contained in some $T_{i(j)}$, and elements $h_j\in R_j$ which are nonzerodivisors and satisfy $W_j\cap b^{-1}(U)=D(h_j)$. Here a nonzerodivisor means multiplication by $h_j$ on $R_j$ is injective, and $D(h_j)$ denotes the set of prime ideals not containing $h_j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The open $b^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense, meaning $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_{b^{-1}(U)}$ is injective for its open inclusion $j$. The equations $h_j$ locally generate one effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with zero set $T\setminus b^{-1}(U)$. If $U$ is empty, $T$ may be chosen empty and both the decomposition and the cover may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, rank separation and affine Cartier reduction; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, boundary principalization paragraph.

proof.text: Choose a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $S$ with $V(\mathcal I)=S\setminus U$ by [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists]. Apply [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier] to its blowup $a:S_0\to S$. Its extended ideal is invertible, its zero set is $S_0\setminus U^0$, where $U^0=a^{-1}(U)$, and $U^0$ is scheme-theoretically dense. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], $U^0\cong U$, so its pieces $U_i^0$ are still quasi-compact and clopen. Each is constructible in $U^0$: a clopen subset and its complement meet every quasi-compact open in a closed, hence quasi-compact, subset, so both are retrocompact as required by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The base $S_0$ is qcqs by the final assertion of [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, proof paragraphs 2–3; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, boundary principalization and successive blowups.

proof.text: List the finitely many unordered pairs of distinct indices. Starting with $S_0$, for each pair $(i,k)$ apply [lemma-nagata-separate-constructible-closed] to the two clopen subsets of the current preserved open corresponding to $U_i,U_k$. They are closed and constructible, disjoint, and their complements are finite unions of the other quasi-compact pieces. This yields an admissible blowup on which their inverse-image closures are disjoint. The preserved open remains isomorphic to $U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], and the new base remains qcqs by [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus], so the next application has all its hypotheses. Previously achieved disjointness persists: for a continuous map $g$, the closure of $g^{-1}(A)$ is contained in $g^{-1}(\overline A)$, which is closed; inverse images of disjoint closed sets are disjoint. Finite induction therefore gives a tower ending in $T$ where all closures of the inverse images of $U_i$ are pairwise disjoint. If there are no pairs the tower is empty. By repeated [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp], its composite $b:T\to S$ is one $U$-admissible blowup. The same result applied over $S_0$ shows that $T\to S_0$ is $U^0$-admissible (the empty tower is the identity).

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, proof paragraphs 2–3; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, boundary principalization and successive blowups.

proof.text: Apply the further-blowup clause of [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier] to $T\to S_0$. Thus the extended ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_T$ is invertible with zero set $T\setminus b^{-1}(U)$, and $b^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense. Invertibility here means locally free of rank one by [def-nagata-invertible-ideal]. A local free generator maps under the ideal inclusion to a section $h$ of $\mathcal O_T$; multiplication by $h$ is injective because both the chosen trivialization and the ideal inclusion are injective. Hence $\mathcal J$ is an effective Cartier ideal by [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal].

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, proof paragraphs 2–3; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, boundary principalization and successive blowups.

proof.text: Put $A_i=b^{-1}(U_i)$ and $T_i=\overline {A_i}$ as subsets of $T$. Scheme-theoretic density implies topological density: on an open disjoint from $b^{-1}(U)$, the injection $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_{b^{-1}(U)}$ forces the structure sheaf to be zero, hence that open has no points (each point has a nonzero local ring). Since the family is finite, $T=\overline{\bigcup_i A_i}=\bigcup_i\overline {A_i}$. The $T_i$ are pairwise disjoint closed subsets by step 2, and each has closed complement $\bigcup_{k\ne i}T_k$, hence is open. Give each its open subscheme structure. Closure in the open $b^{-1}(U)$ is computed by intersection with closure in $T$; there $A_i$ is already closed. Consequently $T_i\cap b^{-1}(U)=A_i$. If $U=\varnothing$, take $\mathcal I=0$ in step 1: the zero ideal is finite type, and the density injection into the zero sheaf forces its blowup to be empty. All pieces and the affine covering may then be empty, including when the index set is empty.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, proof paragraphs 2–3; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, boundary principalization and successive blowups.

proof.text: On the generator neighbourhoods of $\mathcal J$ from step 3, refine by the open pieces $T_i$, and choose affine neighbourhoods of all points contained in these intersections. Affine neighbourhoods exist by the definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Each resulting $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ has a generator $h\in R$ of the same ideal $\mathcal J|_W$; restriction preserves the injectivity of multiplication by $h$, and taking sections is left exact, so $h$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R$. By the definition of the zero set of an ideal in an affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $W\cap b^{-1}(U)=W\setminus V(h)=D(h)$. The base $T$ is quasi-compact by step 2, so finitely many of these affine neighbourhoods cover it. Their equations generate the one global effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal J$ and have exactly the required zero set. Quasi-separatedness of $T$ was also retained at every step.
